batch_strategy: Jointly freeze these 32 distinct supplied candidate IDs and their supplied current-model predictions. Prioritize gaps in solvent-response curves, a crossed scaffold/loading comparison prompted by recent feedback, and controlled loading contrasts. Judge learning value from measured endpoints and chemical context; treat single-predictor quantile widths as secondary evidence.

choices.reason: m116 at 10/1 and 52.55 mg fills an intermediate ratio before its large measured 50/1 response. Together with the selected low-loading 20/1 point, it locates curvature in this neutral dimethoxy-aromatic response.

m116 at 20/1 and 52.55 mg connects directly to its identical-loading 50/1 observation. The existing 20/1 observation uses twice the sample mass, so this label helps separate solvent-response curvature from loading transfer.

m116 at 50/1 and 157.65 mg tests whether its large low-loading response persists. With measured low-loading m116, measured high-loading m123, and the selected low-loading m123 row, it completes a nearly mass-matched scaffold-by-loading comparison.

m123 at 50/1 and 52.65 mg supplies the missing low-loading counterpart to its recent high-loading observation. Its loading nearly matches measured low-loading m116, allowing their contrasting behavior to be examined without the original loading confound.

m122 at 50/1 extends its measured 20/1 low-loading anchor. Comparison with the related bromodimethoxy scaffold tests transfer across methoxy substitution patterns, with loading differences retained explicitly.

m110 at 50/1 and 56.3 mg extends its same-loading 20/1 observation. This trimethoxy aromatic tests whether adding an acceptor predicts the weak-eluent slope better than analogies to the contrasting dimethoxy scaffolds.

m40 at 20/1 fills a solvent-ratio gap for an ordinary naphthyl ketone. Its measured 50/1 low-loading endpoint is much later than its strong-eluent records, so this intermediate label can constrain curvature, although loading differs from that anchor.

m41 at 20/1 and 49.3 mg extends an identical-loading 5/1 observation toward the weak-eluent region highlighted by its recent 50/1 failure. It tests where the rise develops while allowing comparison with existing higher-loading endpoints.

m32 at 50/1 extends the para-methyl aromatic ketone beyond its measured intermediate conditions. Together with the measured meta isomer and selected ortho isomer, it tests positional transfer of weak-eluent slopes while acknowledging differing loading settings.

m44 at 50/1 and 102.6 mg adds the ortho-methyl ketone endpoint at nearly the loading of the measured meta isomer. It tests whether steric environment changes the condition-response curve rather than only baseline retention.

Acetophenone m42 at 50/1 provides the unsubstituted reference for the selected methyl-substituted ketones. It extends an existing same-loading 20/1 observation and constrains transfer across a common neutral carbonyl family.

m125 at 2/1, 100 mg, and 300 uL DCM supplies a missing ratio between measured 1/1 and 5/1 conditions. Its paired 500 uL experiment isolates recorded loading-solvent volume at fixed sample mass and eluent ratio.

The 500 uL counterpart to the selected m125 300 uL row tests a loading-volume effect that current predictions barely distinguish. Measured 1/1 contrasts motivate this controlled test at a new ratio without assuming that their differences are fully reproducible.

Ethyl acetoacetate m82 at 20/1 tests transfer from its measured 5/1 response and the methyl analogue's measured 20/1 behavior. It distinguishes ester-substituent effects on completion from a generic multi-carbonyl correction.

tert-Butyl acetoacetate m25 at 50/1 extends its same-loading 10/1 observation. Comparison with the long completion measured for methyl acetoacetate tests whether ester substitution changes weak-eluent tail growth.

Benzyl-substituted beta-ketoester m78 at 10/1 fills a fixed-loading condition gap before its measured 20/1 and 50/1 responses. It teaches the response shape leading to consistently large weak-eluent endpoints.

m92 at 20/1 and 115.5 mg adjudicates the large contrast between measured low- and high-loading settings. This middle loading tests whether the disparity follows a usable response or reflects variability beyond the recorded features.

Aliphatic unsaturated aldehyde m53 at 20/1 extends its identical-loading 2/1 observation toward a late measured 50/1 endpoint at a different loading. It adds a non-aromatic carbonyl response with potentially distinct completion curvature.

m183 at 50/1 extends its same-loading 20/1 observation. Its recent 10/1 outcome had nearly correct predicted onset but underestimated completion, motivating direct supervision of both endpoints farther along this ordinary aldehyde curve.

Dialdehyde m191 at 2/1 fills the response between measured strong-eluent conditions and its same-loading 5/1 observation. It tests how a second aromatic aldehyde changes early completion growth relative to monoaldehyde controls.

Primary benzylic alcohol m135 at 2/1 and 49 mg localizes the rise leading to its identical-loading 5/1 observation. Recent high-loading feedback showed separate onset and completion errors, strengthening the value of an earlier condition anchor.

m207 at 5/1 and 234 mg tests the higher-loading continuation of markedly different low- and middle-loading observations. The result can identify useful loading signal without assuming that either earlier value defines the whole curve.

Primary alcohol m204 at 1/1 supplies a stronger-eluent anchor before measured 2/1 and same-loading 5/1 conditions. It tests whether its large later response begins already at 1/1 and how that behavior transfers across primary alcohol scaffolds.
m206 at 2/1 and 50 mg builds an identical-loading 2/1-to-5/1 comparison. An existing middle-loading 2/1 observation provides an additional loading reference for this fused-aromatic primary alcohol.
Oxime m11 at 10/1 fills an intermediate condition between same-loading 5/1 and 50/1 observations. It tests the onset of the large donor/acceptor response in a functional group distinct from alcohols.

Tertiary amino-acrylate m19 in pure EA provides a missing strong-eluent baseline at the loading of measured 1/1 and 2/1 records. It separates early basic-scaffold retention from subsequent ratio dependence.
Phenylpyridine m211 at 50/1 extends its fixed low-loading series through 5/1, 10/1, and 20/1. It tests whether this sterically substituted aza-aromatic maintains its moderate slope at weaker eluent.
Quinoline m216 at 1/1 supplies an early condition before its steep measured response at 2/1 and 5/1. It helps distinguish aza-aromatic baseline retention from later solvent-response growth.

Methyl anthranilate m104 at 10/1 and 116.8 mg fills a fixed-loading gap between measured 5/1 and 20/1 conditions. The label tests a plateau versus a developing rise and calibrates transfer from related amino-esters.

Cinnamic acid m173 at 1/1 fills a fixed-loading, fixed-plug-volume gap between pure EA and 2/1 observations. Its predicted completion is slightly below the measured pure-EA endpoint, making this intermediate useful for testing acid-tail interpolation.

Nitroalcohol m200 in pure EA tests whether substantial completion tailing already occurs under the strongest supplied mobile phase. Measured 1/1 and same-loading 2/1 records show long intervals but do not establish this baseline.

Beta-ketonitrile m47 at 2/1 and 100 mg extends its same-loading pure-EA observation toward a higher-loading 5/1 record. It tests condition transfer for a nitrile-carbonyl arrangement distinct from aromatic nitriles and beta-ketoesters.

hypotheses.content: The contrasting 50/1 behavior and opposite historical acquisition errors for m116 and m123 reflect a scaffold-by-eluent interaction rather than being explained entirely by their different sample loadings.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The crossed loading comparison and intermediate m116 ratios distinguish structural solvent-response signal from loading transfer. Related methoxy aromatics test whether the resulting correction generalizes within this neutral family.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: When both scaffolds have 50/1 labels near 53 and 158 mg, do their endpoints remain separated, and where does the low-loading m116 response bend between 10/1, 20/1, and 50/1?

hypotheses.content: Ordinary aromatic ketones require substitution-specific weak-eluent response curves; substantial failures are not confined to unusual heteroatom environments.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Acetophenone, methyl positional isomers, and a naphthyl ketone provide interpretable supervision for common structure-condition relationships. These labels can improve routine-row accuracy and constrain spillover from corrections learned on strongly interacting compounds.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do methyl position and fused aromatic structure change the location or magnitude of the weak-eluent rise after accounting for recorded loading?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl and ester topology changes solvent-response curvature and affects onset and completion differently; a common multi-acceptor correction cannot reliably calibrate both endpoints.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected beta-ketoesters, substituted beta-ketoester, and dialdehyde fill different parts of response curves. They teach endpoint-specific effects of functional-group arrangement rather than treating acceptor count or elution-interval width as sufficient.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does ethyl acetoacetate at 20/1 approach the methyl analogue's completion volume, and do tert-butyl substitution, benzyl substitution, and a second aldehyde produce distinct response shapes?

hypotheses.content: Recorded loading variables may contain useful scaffold- and ratio-dependent signal, but they are insufficient to explain all endpoint variation; reproducibility of particular loading effects remains unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The fixed-mass m125 plug-volume pair isolates one recorded variable at a new ratio. The m92 middle loading and m207 higher loading test whether other apparent effects extend reproducibly. Identical-condition variability cautions against fitting a universal loading slope.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At m125 2/1 and 100 mg, does changing DCM volume from 300 to 500 uL shift either endpoint? Do new m92 and m207 loadings support smooth conditional responses or expose variation beyond the catalog features?

hypotheses.content: Donor-containing scaffolds differ in where their solvent-response rise occurs, and changes in onset need not track changes in completion.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Earlier alcohol anchors and an intermediate oxime condition locate response changes across donor environments. This should help the model learn separate V1 and V2 relationships instead of deriving completion from onset through one shared adjustment.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which donor scaffolds begin their main rise at 1/1-to-2/1, 2/1-to-5/1, or later, and does that rise primarily move onset, completion, or both?

hypotheses.content: Nitrogen-containing scaffolds require context-specific PE/EA slopes, distinguishing basic amines and aza-aromatics, neutral nitriles, and amino-carbonyl environments.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The batch adds a strong-eluent amino-acrylate baseline, an early quinoline point, a fixed-loading phenylpyridine extension, and missing amino-ester and ketonitrile intermediates. These comparisons constrain transfer between nitrogen environments with different interaction chemistry.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Can the model transfer response shape within nitrogen subfamilies while retaining different baselines and slopes associated with electronic and steric context?

feedback_interpretation: The latest outcomes shift emphasis toward coherent local comparisons. At acquisition, the recent m116 50/1 row was underpredicted by 21.87/26.70 mL, whereas the m123 50/1 row was overpredicted by 5.72/16.68 mL. These are historical errors, not current-model residuals. Their contrasting measured behavior motivates the crossed loading comparison and methoxy-family extensions. An ordinary m41 ketone also had substantial underprediction, so failure repair includes common neutral families. Recent m135 and m183 outcomes had nearly correct predicted onset but underestimated completion, reinforcing separate endpoint calibration. Conversely, recent m80 outcomes had short measured intervals; additional generic multi-acceptor tail corrections would be poorly justified. Loading-only explanations remain uncertain because some records differ despite identical catalog conditions. The m125 pair therefore tests a controlled contrast without presuming that every disparity is a loading effect. Finally, the latest acid-bearing m45 outcome is at 20/1, not a repeat of its anomalous 50/1 record. Its plausible endpoints do not validate the near-zero, reversed 50/1 label or establish a physical transition.
batch_rationale: The batch concentrates measurements where they can discriminate between explanations and fill response curves. Its central experiment completes a nearly mass-matched m116/m123 scaffold-by-loading comparison at 50/1, while two intermediate m116 conditions locate solvent-response curvature. Related methoxy aromatics test transfer beyond that pair. Common aromatic ketones and aliphatic and aromatic aldehydes cover routine Row chemistry, including regions highlighted by recent failures. Multi-carbonyl rows fill topology and ratio gaps, and the m125 pair isolates loading-solvent volume without changing sample mass or mobile phase. Alcohol, oxime, nitrogen-containing, acid, and nitroalcohol rows extend interaction coverage through missing baselines or intermediate conditions. Existing measured anchors make these same-molecule selections informative; most selected condition tuples are absent from the measured set. The selection does not maximize predicted elution volumes, interval widths, or quantile widths. Many supplied V2 lower quantiles are zero, and some V1 quantiles cross the median, so these single-predictor outputs are not treated as calibrated epistemic uncertainty. The expected benefit is better learning of conditional structure-response relationships and separate V1/V2 behavior across routine and difficult portions of the Row-distribution.
